ewhc/ch/2015/1840.rationale: This case is directly on point for the question of the shape of a taxi as a trade mark. The proceedings concern Community Trade Mark No 951871 and UK registered trade mark No 2440659, both of which depict versions of the London black cab (the Fairway and TX1) — i.e., shape/design marks for taxis — with infringement and passing-off claims based on the appearance of those cabs. Paragraph 70 quotes Mr Roberts describing the trade mark issue as "the circumstances under which manufacturers may obtain a perpetual monopoly in the shape of their goods", which squarely frames the question of whether a taxi's shape can function as a trade mark. Although this particular judgment is an interlocutory ruling on survey evidence, the underlying dispute is centrally about the protectability/enforcement of the London black cab shape as a trade mark, making it a directly on-point authority for the research question.
